newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says Zaire mission could end early.
newsitem.headline: France says Zaire mission could end early.

text.p: France said on Saturday it was preparing to deploy troops to Zaire as part of a multinational force and added that the mission might end before the March 31 expiration of its U.N. mandate.
"Planning relative to deployment and evaluation missions is under way," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

"The commitment of the multinational force, which should include a French contingent of about 1,000 men, expires in principle on March 31 but its goals might be achieved before that date," the ministry added.

The Security Council authorised late on Friday the deployment of a Canadian-led multinational force to take food, water and medicines to primarily Hutu Rwandan refugees stranded in eastern Zaire by fighting between Zairean forces and Tutsi rebels.
In an unexpected development, however, refugees were streaming back into Rwanda from Zaire by the hundreds of thousands on Saturday, witnesses said.

The reverse exodus, which began after the flight of Hutu gunmen who had persuaded or forced refugees not to go home, could signal a breakthrough in humanitarian efforts to keep the refugees from starving.
France said it was pleased by the voluntary return of refugees to Rwanda but was also delighted by United Nations approval of the humanitarian rescue mission for the remaining refugees.

It thanked U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali for his work in attaining approval of the plan, Canada for agreeing to lead the mission and the United States for agreeing to contribute troops. Other countries to have pledged troops include Britain, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Senegal, South Africa and Spain.
The statement gave no indication of when French troops might begin arriving in Zaire.
French defence officials said earlier this week they could have 600 troops in place within 24 hours of U.N. approval of the mission and another 600 troops within 48 hours of U.N. action.
Defence sources said on Saturday, however, that that they did not expect French troops to begin heading for Zaire before Monday.
